Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m one of the perinatal mental-health clinicians here. I’ll be guiding you through a short screening called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS**. It’s simply a way for us to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived, because the postpartum period can bring a lot of unexpected emotions along with the joy.  

Everything you share is confidential, and this is a judgment-free space. We’ll go through ten questions about the past seven days; you can answer in your own words, and we’ll take it at your pace. Ready to begin?

First question: Over the last week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

Hi Sarah. I’ve still been able to laugh—maybe not quite as easily as before the baby, but if something’s genuinely funny I’ll chuckle. It just feels like it takes a little more effort, and the laughs don’t last as long.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Yeah… most of the time I can still laugh if something’s really funny, but it doesn’t come as naturally as it used to. Sometimes I’ll smile or give a little chuckle, but it feels kind of forced, like I’m doing it because I know I should, not because it just bubbles up the way it did before I had the baby.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still look forward to some things—like my morning coffee or when my sister visits—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it used to be. It’s more like “that’ll be nice” instead of really counting down the hours.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. Like if the baby’s fussy and won’t settle, I’ll think maybe I’m not doing something right or I’m missing some “mom instinct” everyone else seems to have. Most of the time I can talk myself down, but it still pops into my head more than I’d like.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll suddenly feel tense, like a tightness in my chest, even when nothing’s really happening. I’ll catch myself worrying that the baby’s breathing sounds different or that I forgot to do something important, and then I have to take a few breaths to settle. It usually passes pretty quickly, but it shows up out of nowhere a couple of times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Every now and then I’ll get this quick wave of fear, like my heart races and I feel shaky, but it’s over in a minute or two. There’s nothing specific I can point to—it just hits and then fades. It’s happened maybe twice this week.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days it feels like the little stuff—laundry, dishes, a fussy baby—all piles up at once and I think, “How am I supposed to keep doing this?” I still manage, but it’s like I’m running right at my limit and one extra thing could tip the balance.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

No, it’s not that I’m too unhappy to sleep—most nights I drift off okay. Every so often I’ll lie there thinking about everything I need to do tomorrow or replaying something I wish I’d done differently, and it takes me an extra half-hour to settle, but I wouldn’t say it’s because I’m really unhappy.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel sad some of the time—like a heavy feeling that sits on my chest for a while, especially in the evenings when the baby’s finally down and the house is quiet. It’s not every day, but I’d say most days this week I’ve had at least a spell where I just felt kind of low and weepy.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… I’ve cried a couple of times this week. It’s not that I’m sobbing all day or anything, but when everything feels a bit much—like yesterday when she wouldn’t nap and I couldn’t get the bottles washed—I just teared up and couldn’t stop the tears for a few minutes.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I might feel overwhelmed or tearful, but hurting myself has never crossed my mind.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 13: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note

**Presenting symptoms endorsed:**
- Diminished ability to laugh and find enjoyment (Q1, Q2)
- Daily low mood, “heavy feeling,” weepiness most evenings (Q8)
- Crying spells when overwhelmed (Q9)
- Unwarranted self-blame regarding infant care (Q3)
- Episodic, unexplained anxiety/tight chest several times daily; two brief panic-like episodes this week (Q4, Q5)
- Feeling “at limit,” easily overwhelmed by routine tasks (Q6)

**Symptoms denied:**
- Sleep disturbance secondary to low mood (Q7)
- Any self-harm thoughts (Q10)

**Pattern impression:**
Responses reveal mild-to-moderate depressive features (anhedonia, tearfulness, guilt) co-occurring with episodic anxiety/panic. Functioning maintained but with perceived narrow margin of coping reserve.

**Risk flags:**
- Frequent sadness and crying spells
- Unwarranted guilt re: parenting competence
- Recurrent, unexplained anxiety/panic symptoms
- No safety concerns (no suicidal or self-harm ideation)

**Screening conclusion:**
Subthreshold-to-mild range symptoms consistent with postpartum depression and anxiety; continued monitoring and formal clinical assessment recommended to rule out major peripartum mood/anxiety disorder.
